h: לַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב, ד׳ Tu B'Av, 4

p: "There were no festive days for Yisrael
on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out, and so on,
and dance in the vineyards, and so on.
'Go out and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon,
upon the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding
and on the day of the gladness of his heart.'
'On the day of his wedding' — this is the Giving of the Torah;
'and on the day of the gladness of his heart' —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."
because it has in it pardon and forgiveness,
and it is the day on which the second Tablets were given;
אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב מַאי הוּא
but the fifteenth of Av — what is it?
Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel:
It is the day on which the tribes were permitted
"This means that it is a Yom Tov."
שְׁתֵּי קוּשְׁיוֹת עַל חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב
two difficulties about the fifteenth of Av:
בִּשְׁלָמָא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא יוֹם טוֹב
granted that Yom HaKippurim is a Yom Tov
because it has in it pardon and forgiveness,
that the second Tablets were given on it;
אֲבָל חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב מַאי הוּא
but the fifteenth of Av, what is it —
for what reason is it a Yom Tov?
And also, why should it be even greater
Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel,
יוֹם שֶׁהוּתְּרוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים לָבוֹא זֶה בָּזֶה
"the day on which the tribes were permitted to marry into one another,"
and with this the first difficulty is answered;
and this is what Tosafos said:
"This means that it is a Yom Tov."
There still remains the second difficulty:
"the day on which the tribe of Binyamin was permitted
is from the wording of the Gemara in the second reason,
אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
"Said Rav Yosef, said Rav Nachman," opening with "said":
for if it were a different answer
simply "Rav Yosef said in the name of Rav Nachman,"
in the manner of the Talmud's discussions
and like the other statements in the Gemara there.
to answer the second difficulty mentioned above.
"and on the day of the gladness of his heart —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash";
וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְכָאן
and seemingly this has no connection at all to here,
even according to the explanation of the Bartenura,
שֶׁחוֹזֵר גַּם כֵּן עַל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
that it too refers to Yom HaKippurim,
on which the dedication of the Beis HaMikdash took place;
for from the wording of the Mishnah,
"this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,"
the implication is the building itself
Now, in the pasuk it says
"Behold, there is a festival of Hashem in Shiloh
and, "Behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out
to dance in the dances," etc.
which festival it was, year after year,
on which they went out to dance in the dances;
and he said that it was possibly on Yom HaKippurim,
when the daughters of Yisrael would go out
only in Shiloh and in Yerushalayim
What appears in all this is as follows.
the statement of our Sages, of blessed memory,
"'Upon the crown with which his mother crowned him' —
and He did not cease cherishing her
That is, when there shines forth in Knesses Yisrael
which is the aspect of Imma Ila'ah, as is known;
and this is the illumination of the mochin
in the inner point of the heart
which joins the mind and the heart,
the aspect of Chochmah and Binah.
like a crown upon the head;
and this is the aspect of "the crown
with which his mother crowned him" — precisely his mother.
However, there are two aspects in this.
the shining of Da'as in the souls of Yisrael
by way of the illumination of an awakening from Above;
and this is the meaning of
"'on the day of his wedding' — this is the Giving of the Torah,"
שֶׁאָז הָיָה נִשְׁפָּע הַדַּעַת בִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
for then Da'as flowed into Knesses Yisrael
by way of an awakening from Above.
This was at the Giving of the Torah
עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
through Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who was the totality of the Da'as
of the generation of the wilderness,
who are called the "generation of knowledge";
through the Giving of the Torah,
which was then "engraved on the Tablets,"
together with the recognition of the illumination of G-dliness,
upon the tablet of their heart.
And this is called "the day of his wedding":
and sanctified us with His Torah,
and planted eternal life within us,
like the betrothal of the groom to the bride.
And there is one more aspect,
which is called "on the day of the gladness of his heart,"
and this is "the building of the Beis HaMikdash":
when the souls of Yisrael merit
and in recognition of His providence, may He be blessed,
in the innermost point of their heart —
זֶה נִקְרָא בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּעֶצֶם
this is called the building of the Beis HaMikdash in essence,
as they, of blessed memory, said
with which heaven and earth were created,
'He filled him with the spirit of G-d,
and with knowledge and with every craft.'"
And about this they, of blessed memory, said
it is as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days";
is in essence the building of the Beis HaMikdash.
"on the day of the gladness of his heart,"
for, as it were, Hashem Yisbarach receives joy
when the awakening of Da'as comes from their side.
And this applies also to each individual soul in particular,
when he exerts himself with his whole soul
as they, of blessed memory, said
that the Holy One, blessed is He, exults and rejoices
when the soul of a tzaddik comes to Him.
"the day on which the tribes were permitted
from one tribe to another tribe"
was because each and every tribe
יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּחִינָה מְיוּחֶדֶת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
has a distinct aspect of its own
in the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
in the blessing of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
for he blessed each tribe on its own
according to the measure of its aspect.
Therefore each tribe on its own
with regard to the bull for an error of the community
for each tribe on its own.
Now, the command "an inheritance shall not pass"
is stated in the Torah in the language,
"This is the thing that Hashem has commanded"
and we have already spoken of this:
שֶׁנִּזְכָּר בִּנְבוּאַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
where the prophecy of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
to the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
as does all the rest of the Torah,
which is called by his name,
"Remember the Torah of Moshe My servant."
Therefore it is stated in the language,
"This is the thing that Hashem has commanded,"
is solely from the command of Hashem Yisbarach
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him.
כִּי בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
was the Da'as of all of Yisrael,
that is, the aspect of the surrounding light
for the entire community of Yisrael as one;
in the blessing of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him
"And this is what their father spoke to them,
for he also included them all as one,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִכְלָלִים כָּל הַבְּחִינוֹת זֶה בָּזֶה
so that all the aspects would be included in one another
עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַדַּעַת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
through the aspect of Da'as, as mentioned above.
in the Chamber of Hewn Stone,
drawn from all of Yisrael together,
"For from Tziyon shall go forth Torah";
and, "You shall arise and go up
to the place that Hashem will choose"
And it was specifically to them
that Hashem Yisbarach gave the insight
and they permitted the tribes to marry into one another
specifically in the place of the Mikdash;
and this took place at the time of
the fifteenth of the month of Av,
as we spoke of this on Shabbos Chazon:
was created with the letter tes,
that is, the aspect of "the light, that it was good,"
only that its goodness is hidden within it,
as it is written in the holy Zohar
since the six days of Creation to be revealed in it;
which is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
which brings forth the wisdom of the Torah
from the understanding of the heart,
and knowledge is pleasant to your soul."
And especially on the fifteenth of the month of Av,
for then "the moon stands in its fullness";
and therefore this day too was
which is the revelation of the surrounding light,
and specifically in the place of the Mikdash,
And also in the future to come
will be ready for the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא יג, טו).
as it says in the Pesikta (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana 13:15),
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה יוֹם טוֹב גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ
so that there will be no Yom Tov greater than it.
This is because then there will be
in the revelation of the hidden light;
and then the Holy One, blessed is He, is destined
to make the dance for the tzaddikim
"And it shall be said on that day," etc.
And it is in this very month that
"the joy of our heart has ceased;
our dancing has turned to mourning"
because we were not worthy of this
And before this pasuk it says
"The elders have ceased from the gate" —
who are those who sit at the gate;
whose way it was to learn with a melody,
and let it be like a song"
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁבַת מְשׂוֹשׂ לִבֵּנוּ
And through this "the joy of our heart has ceased,"
which is "the gladness of his heart";
and "our dancing has turned to mourning" —
that is, the aspect of the dance
that was designated for this month;
and "the crown of our head has fallen"
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הָאוֹר מַקִּיף כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
which is the aspect of the surrounding light, as mentioned above.
was created with the letter ches,
as it says in Sefer Yetzirah
and the statement of our Sages, of blessed memory, is known
"They make a hump on the roof of the ches,
כְּלוֹמַר חַי הוּא בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
as if to say: He lives in the heights of the world."
That is, the month of Tammuz
was prepared for receiving the first Tablets,
which are the aspect of eternal life,
that is, the aspect of the revelation
of the illumination of the Written Torah,
שֶׁהָיָה חָרוּת עַל הַלּוּחוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
which was engraved on the Tablets, as mentioned above.
And because the sin brought it about
only in the heights of the world.
to attain the aspect of eternal life
עַל יְדֵי הָאוֹת ט׳ שֶׁבַּחוֹדֶשׁ אָב
through the letter tes of the month of Av,
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
he will merit the revelation of "the light, that it was good,"
hidden away since the six days of Creation.
And through this we can attain
the aspect of the revelation of the Written Torah,
As we spoke of this on Shabbos Kodesh:
that through "so that it may be good for you"
which is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
it is possible to attain also the aspect of
"so that your days may be lengthened"
"in the world that is entirely long"
which is the aspect of the Written Torah
that stands in the heights of the world.
Now, it says there in the Gemara,
according to the version of the Ein Yaakov,
the beautiful, those of distinguished lineage,
And it says in the writings of the Arizal
that they correspond to the four letters
of the Name Havayah, blessed is He.
And the unattractive and the poor
correspond to the letter yud of the Name.
And certainly the Gemara did not bring this
rather, they allude to supernal secrets.
It is like what is said
at the Splitting of the Sea
and all the women went out after her
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן מְרַמֵּז לְסוֹדוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים
This too alludes to supernal secrets,
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי שְׁנֵי מִינֵי כְּלֵי זֶמֶר הָאֵלּוּ
That is, these two kinds of musical instruments
which are the totality of the kelipah.
which has the numerical value of tof, drum;
וְהַקְּלִיפָּה זוֹ הוּא שֶׁל עֶצֶב וִילָלָה
and this kelipah is one of sadness and wailing,
as they, of blessed memory, said
"She began to wail over him with her voice."
And with the study of Torah she'b'al peh
which is one of a joy of frivolity
Now, at the Splitting of the Sea
הָיָה גַּם כֵּן הִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁל הָאוֹר מַקִּיף
there was also a revelation of the surrounding light
as is known from the holy Zohar, Beshalach
that the Splitting of the Sea
לָכֵן הָיָה בְּכֹחַ הַנָּשִׁים גַּם כֵּן
Therefore it was within the power even of the women,
to go out with drum and dance,
from the aspect of Da'as, as mentioned above;
and as they, of blessed memory, said
And as is known, there are levels
of the aspect of Iggulim and Yosher, circles and line:
above and below, like the form of a man;
but in the aspect of Iggulim,
that is, in the revelation of the surrounding light,
there is no distinction of levels,
and small and great alike are there,
able to reach the highest level.
וְלָכֵן גַּם בִּזְמַן חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב
Therefore also at the time of the fifteenth of Av,
which was likewise the time designated
for the revelation of the surrounding light, as mentioned above,
אָז גַּם כֵּן תִּשְׂמַח בְּתוּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמָחוֹל
then too "the maiden of Yisrael shall rejoice in dance"
that allude to the realm Above.
that of Rav Yosef in the name of Rav Nachman,
"the day on which the tribe of Binyamin was permitted
It is learned from the pasuk mentioned above:
"Behold, there is a festival to Hashem in Shiloh
and if the daughters of Shiloh come out
on the day of the fifteenth of Av,
Now, the permission for the tribe of Binyamin
also came about by virtue of
the shining of the aspect of Da'as
at the time designated for this,
"Why should a tribe be lacking today from Yisrael?"
For from the aspect of Da'as,
שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּאֶחָד
which includes all the souls of Yisrael as one,
it is impossible that there be lacking
from the twelve tribes of Yeshurun,
"It is a tradition that a tribe will not be wiped out";
correspond to the twelve diagonal boundaries
In the first year, at this time,
this began to stir in their hearts:
"What shall we do for wives for those who remain," etc.
and the Holy One, blessed is He, opened their eyes
that they should seize wives for themselves
from the dances held on this day.
And the following year as well,
the Holy One, blessed is He, opened the eyes
to find an exposition from the word "from us" —
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִתִּירָם לָבוֹא בַּקָּהָל
and thereby it permitted them to enter the congregation
so that the holiness of the tribe would be made whole
that the holiness of the day caused them
עַד שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
to the point that there were no festive days for Yisrael
like the fifteenth of Av and Yom HaKippurim.
וְעַל זֶה גַּם יָבוֹא עַל נָכוֹן
And with this the pasuk too is properly understood:
"upon the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding" —
this is the Giving of the Torah,
"and the day of the gladness of his heart" —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
that is, the fifteenth of Av,
in keeping with our words above.
